newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS flights to Tallinn allowed till Nov 22.
newsitem.headline: SAS flights to Tallinn allowed till Nov 22.

text.p: Scandinavian and Estonian air traffic authorities have reached agreement on extending until November 22 the current flying rights between Scandinavia and Tallinn, Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) said in a statement.
SAS and Estonian Air, majority-owned by Maersk, had warned of a temporary halt to flights between Tallinn, Copenhagen and Stockholm if the row over the routes was not resolved.
SAS at present flies once daily from Stockholm and twice daily from Copenhagen to Tallinn, the Estonia capital.
The dispute began when Estonia asked SAS to cut the Copenhagen flights to one a day as Estonian Air wanted to resume flights to the Danish capital.
The Estonians also refused SAS permission to boost its Stockholm flights to twice daily.
Estonia says there is too much capacity already on these routes, an argument rejected by SAS.

"From the Scandinavian side we have said we are willing to accept Estonian Air's whole traffic programme, but it is totally unacceptable for SAS to reduce its own traffic programme from Copenhagen to benefit Estonian Air," SAS said on Friday.
"The capacity is needed, and the Estonian authorities' demand to regulate the traffic is incompatible with ambitions to liberalise air tarffic policy."
Maersk won the right in May this year to buy a stake in Estonian Air but the privatisation also interested SAS.
